- When sentiment turns negative or shows sharp decline (especially after a spike), model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast lag and adjust downward bias.
- If sentiment remains positive but news volume drops, model often overestimates future price — reduce forecast peak and apply mean reversion toward recent history.
- After a strong upward spike in sentiment, model frequently overshoots and forecasts too high — cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high or use sentiment decay to dampen.
- When sentiment is flat or mixed, model often fails to capture mean reversion — align forecast with 3–5 day moving average of history.
- If news volume is low, model tends to overreact to sentiment — reduce forecast sensitivity to sentiment change and favor historical trend.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is weak but price is trending up — adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment is below 0.5 and price is rising.
- Forecast should not exceed 3–5% above or below 30-day moving average unless sentiment is strongly bullish/bearish and news volume is high.
